why: LANDED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R8): `ParameterBuilder::mandatory` returns `Result<_, DeclarationError>` now, rclrs's error type, so a ported `match` on its error compiles. The declaration path is unchanged (`ParameterServer::declare_parameter`); its `SetParameterResult` is mapped to name each case it conflated -- `TypeMismatch` there meant AlreadyDeclared, `InvalidRange` meant either InvalidRange or InitialValueOutOfRange. `read_only` with no default is rclrs's `NoValueAvailable` (new variant). What still differs is the variant SET (`server.rs`'s `DeclarationError` doc): ours adds StorageFull / NameTooLong (caller-owned storage) and has no override-mismatch variants, because overrides arrive through the set path. `From<DeclarationError> for ParameterError` keeps `?` into an old caller compiling. Test: `builder_terminals_report_declaration_errors`. PRIOR ROW: phase-428 W6 remainder (2026-09-06) — ledgered because the correlator's return-type comparison became a VERDICT. Return type differs in ONE name and nothing else: rclrs returns `Result<MandatoryParameter<T>, DeclarationError>`, ours (`packages/core/nros-params/src/typed.rs:200`) `Result<MandatoryParameter<'a, 's, T>, ParameterError>`. Same shape, same `Result` (so the discard is already lint-covered by core's own `#[must_use]`), same success type modulo our two lifetimes on a caller-owned store (phase-382). The only real difference is that our error enum is called `ParameterError` where upstream's is `DeclarationError` — a rename we chose and never wrote down, which is exactly what this ledger is for. RFC-0036 forbids recording a preference as a divergence, so the honest verdict is `rename`, and the disposition is ADOPT: nothing about an RTOS motivates the different word. Covers `optional` and `read_only`, which carry pointer rows.
